## $F_{ST}$ from estimated ancestral allele frequencies

On `2024-03-11` we run NGSadmix on variable sites identified from
mappings to the RAD loci. K = 2 was determined as a good fit. The
program not only yields the ancestry proportions of every individual
(the $N \times K$ $Q$ matrix) but also the estimated allele frequencies
in the ancestral populations. Thus, we can estimate the $F_{ST}$
among those presumed ancestral populations. I would do this just to
check that the $F_{ST}$ estimated on `2024-10-10` between what we
call *C. farionis* (most abundant in Langfjordvatn) and *C. pseudofarionis*
(most abundant in Suohpatjavri), namely 0.12, is consistent with
the NGSadmix analysis.

To estimate $F_{ST}$ from estimated allele frequencies, I assume
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in all 315642 loci included in the
NGSadmix analysis. Unfortunately, the number of chromosomes used
in each locus to estimate allele frequencies is unknown. At most,
all 90 individuals had good data, but most probably, the amount
of data is variable across sites. I believe smaller sample sizes
produced downwardly biased estimates. Thus, if I specify the largest
possible sample sizes, I will get the largest estimates.

In any case, the (at most) 90 current individuals represent different
sample sizes of the two ancestral populations assumed when $K=2$.
I assume that the two ancestries are represented by population sizes
proportional to the overall current fraction of the genomes inherited
from them. 

```{r}
source('formulas.R')
K2 <- read.table('../2024-03-11/NGSadmix/ARCTIC.K2.fopt.gz',
                 col.names = c('farionis', 'pseudofarionis'))
Q2 <- read.table('../2024-03-11/NGSadmix/ARCTIC.K2.qopt',
                 col.names = c('farionis', 'psuedofarionis'))
proportions <- colSums(Q2) / dim(Q2)[1]
# maximum number of chromosomes used to estimate frequencies:
n.max <- round(2 * dim(Q2)[1] * proportions)

NumRep <- 250
if (file.exists('FST.Rds')) {
   FST <- readRDS('FST.Rds')
} else {
   FST <- list(
      estimates = sapply(1:5, function(x) WC84w(K2, n.max / x)),
      bootstrap = sapply(1:5, function(x) {
         replicate(NumRep, WC84w(K2[sample(1:dim(K2)[1], 5000, replace = TRUE),], n.max / x))
      })
   )
   saveRDS(FST, file = 'FST.Rds')
}
plot(c(0,6), range(FST[['bootstrap']]), type = 'n',
     axes = FALSE, xlab = 'Assumed sample size',
     ylab = 'FST')
nulldev <- lapply(1:5, function(x) {
   points(rnorm(NumRep, 6 - x, 0.15), FST[['bootstrap']][,x], col = 'gray')
   points(6 - x, FST[['estimates']][x], col = 'red')
})
axis(2)
axis(1, at = 1:5, labels = c('n/5', 'n/4', 'n/3', 'n/2', 'n'))
text(5, 0.15, labels = sprintf("n = (%i, %i)", n.max[1], n.max[2]))
```

Grey dots are bootstrap pseudo-replicates, obtained with only 5000 sites.

The two ancestral populations estimated with NGSadmix on `2024-03-11` seem
to have diverged to an $F_{ST} \leq 0.176$, which is higher than the 0.12
value obtained in `2024-10-10` between current populations. The difference
is unlikely to be due to recent admixture, because on `2024-10-10` only
non-admixed individuals were used. I assume the estimate here is higher for
two reasons: first, because the algorithm in NGSadmix must maximize the
differences between hypotheized ancestral populations. And second, because
estimates with `realSFS` (in `2024-10-10`) may take into account the variable
and limited sample size across sites, while I naively assume all loci have
data in either all or a constant fraction of individuals. The smaller the
fraction, the lower the estimate.

## Nucleotide diversity from the SFS

```{r}
PiTajima <- function(x, folded = TRUE){
   n <- length(x) - 1  # the SFS includes invariable sites and 0 values for i > n/2
   a <- 1:(n/2)
   Theta <- (2/(n * (n-1))) * sum(x[2:(n/2 + 1)] * a * (n - a)) / sum(x)
   return(Theta)
}
Lan.sfs <- scan('../2024-10-10/SFS/Langfjordvatn.sfs', quiet = TRUE)
Suo.sfs <- scan('../2024-10-10/SFS/Suopatjavri.sfs',   quiet = TRUE)
Lan.n <- length(Lan.sfs) - 1
Suo.n <- length(Suo.sfs) - 1
Lan.pi <- PiTajima(Lan.sfs)
Suo.pi <- PiTajima(Suo.sfs)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
barplot(Lan.sfs[1:(1 + Lan.n / 2)], main = 'C. farionis in Langfjordvatn', log = 'y')
text(25, 2.0e+05, bquote(pi==.(Lan.pi)))
barplot(Suo.sfs[1:(1 + Suo.n / 2)], main = 'C. pseudofarionis in Suopatjavri', log = 'y')
text(30, 2.0e+05, bquote(pi==.(Suo.pi)))
```

Both SFSs show a deficit of singletons, which must be due to missed heterozygous
sites or confusion of singletons with sequencing errors. And they show an excess
of high frequency SNPs, which must be the cause of such high $\pi$ values. Note
that I originally included very low-coverage sites in the estimates. Because I
suspected the lack of singletons could be due to such low-coverage sites hiding
heterozygotes, I re-estimated the SFSs in the `2024-10-10` folder, using a minimum
coverage of 4 per individual, and a minimum number of individuals equal to 4/5 the
total number, in each population. The results are essentially the same, with a
small increase of heterozygosity.

The SFSs suggest that invariable sites (first category of the SFS) are about
`r round(Suo.sfs[1] / sum(Suo.sfs[-1]), 2)` or `r round(Lan.sfs[1] / sum(Lan.sfs[-1]), 2)`
times more abundant than variable sites, in *C. pseudofarionis* (Suopatjavri)
and *C. farionis* (Langfjordvatn), respectively.

Assuming the lack of singletons is an artifact, the remaining question is why
there is an excess of high frequency SNPs. Note that part of that excess is shared
or correlated between the two populations (see `2024-10-10`). One possibility is
balancing selection.

## Individual heterozygosity
I want to see if there is any excess of heterozygosity. I will run ANGSD again to obtain
posterior probabilities of genotypes in both populations. I will also obtain posterior
genotype probabilities of the inbred individuals, to see their genomic distribution
of heterozygosity (I expect long runs of excess of heterozygosity). I should
probably run this in Garnatxa.

### With alignments to ddRAD loci

```{bash}
ASM=../2024-10-04/radloci.fa
BAM=../2024-10-04/BAM
# C. farionis only from Langfjordvatn (I exclude S004Cma, S004Cmb, S061Cma and S061Cmb)
if [ ! -e farionis.txt ]; then
   gawk '((NR > 1) && ($3 > 0.95) && ($1 ~ /^L/)){
      print $1
   }' ../2024-10-05/summary.txt | sort > farionis.txt
fi
# C. pseudofarionis only from Suopatjavri (I exclude L131Cmb)
if [ ! -e pseudofarionis.txt ]; then
   gawk '((NR > 1) && ($2 > 0.95) && ($1 ~ /^S/)){
      print $1
   }' ../2024-10-05/summary.txt | sort > pseudofarionis.txt
fi
# Hybrids are L019Cxa, L019Cxb, L088Cma and S023Cxd:
if [ ! -e hybrids.txt ]; then
   gawk '((NR > 1) && ($2 < 0.95) && ($3 < 0.95)){
      print $1
   }' ../2024-10-05/summary.txt | sort > hybrids.txt
fi

if [ ! -d toRadPOST ]; then mkdir toRadPOST; fi
if [ ! -e farionis.sfs ]; then
   ln -s ../2024-10-10/SFS/Langfjordvatn.sfs farionis.sfs
fi
if [ ! -e pseudofarionis.sfs ]; then
   ln -s ../2024-10-10/SFS/Suopatjavri.sfs pseudofarionis.sfs
fi

for pop in farionis pseudofarionis hybrids; do
   if [ ! -e $pop.toRad.list ]; then
      find $BAM -name '*.bam' | grep -f $pop.txt | sort > $pop.toRad.list
   fi
done

if [ ! -e hybrids.sfs ]; then
   # We need to estimate the SFS for the hybrids!
   if [ ! -e hybrids.saf.idx ]; then
      angsd -b hybrids.toRad.list \
            -anc $ASM \
            -ref $ASM \
            -out hybrids \
            -doSaf 1 \
            -doGlf 1 \
            -gl 1 \
            -minMapQ 30 \
            -minQ 20 \
            -only_proper_pairs 1 \
            -baq 1 \
            -minInd 4 \
            -setMinDepthInd 4 \
            -nThreads 4 1> hybrids.saf.log 2> hybrids.saf.err &
   fi
   realSFS -fold 1 \
           -nSites 5000000 \
           hybrids.saf.idx 1> hybrids.sfs 2> hybrids.sfs.log
fi
for pop in farionis pseudofarionis hybrids; do
   MININD=$(( $(cat $pop.txt | wc -l) * 4 / 5 ))
   if [ $MININD -lt 4 ]; then MININD=4; fi
   if [ ! -e toRadPOST/$pop.geno.gz ]; then
      angsd -bam $pop.toRad.list \
            -ref $ASM \
            -out toRadPOST/$pop \
            -doGeno 13 \
            -GL 1 \
            -doPost 3 \
            -skipMissing 0 \
            -pest $pop.sfs \
            -doMajorMinor 1 \
            -doMaf 1 \
            -minMapQ 30 \
            -minQ 20 \
            -baq 1 \
            -minInd $MININD \
            -setMinDepthInd 4 \
            -nThreads 8 1> toRadPOST/$pop.stdout 2> toRadPOST/$pop.stderr
   fi
done
```

### With alignments to reference genome

```{bash}
ASM=../2023-05-15/assembly.fasta
BAM=../2023-05-18/BAM
if [ ! -d toRefPOST ]; then mkdir toRefPOST; fi
for pop in farionis pseudofarionis hybrids; do
   if [ ! -e $pop.toRef.list ]; then
      find $BAM -name '*.bam' | grep -f $pop.txt | sort > $pop.toRef.list
   fi
   MININD=$(( $(cat $pop.txt | wc -l) * 4 / 5 ))
   if [ $MININD -lt 4 ]; then MININD=4; fi
   if [ ! -e toRadPOST/$pop.geno.gz ]; then
      angsd -bam $pop.toRef.list \
            -ref $ASM \
            -out toRefPOST/$pop \
            -doGeno 13 \
            -GL 1 \
            -doPost 3 \
            -skipMissing 0 \
            -pest $pop.sfs \
            -doMajorMinor 1 \
            -doMaf 1 \
            -minMapQ 30 \
            -minQ 20 \
            -baq 1 \
            -minInd $MININD \
            -setMinDepthInd 4 \
            -nThreads 8 1> toRefPOST/$pop.stdout 2> toRefPOST/$pop.stderr
   fi
done
```
